target_customer: Developers who build MCP servers and want them to push events to AI agents
problem: MCP servers are pull-only, so agents in Claude Code, Codex or Cursor must poll or need harness specific code to react to events.
business_model: Developer SDK and hosted event delivery service (pricing not stated)

founders.name: Eric Levine
previous_startups: Berbix (YC S18, acquired by Socure in 2023 for a reported 70M dollars)
founders.background_notes: Site copyright is held by Clawvisor Inc.

technical_complexity.rationale: An event relay and SDK across several agent harnesses is mostly integration work, though harness behavior changes quickly.

defensibility.rationale: The idea builds on the open MCP Events proposal and rivals such as the Hookdeck bridge, and harness makers can add native wake support.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Search results show Claude Code channel notifications and an MCP Events spec in progress in 2026, so platforms were already building the wedge.

market_need_then: Open Claude Code issues in 2026 request external wake signals and push notifications from MCP servers, and an MCP Triggers and Events working group was chartered in March 2026, showing real demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short, metaphorical: The wake-up call for AI agents

branding.brand_signature: The wake-up call for AI agents tagline

brand_strength.rationale: The name matches the product, but the company is new and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Wakeshift is a Spring 2026 YC company from a repeat founder with a prior acquisition. It is too new for an outcome. The main risk visible in sources is that MCP Events standards and agent harness vendors may provide the wake feature natively.
notes: Searches for outcome, funding and brand returned nothing about Wakeshift. Related projects (Hookdeck MCP Events bridge, Agent Wake Protocol, Claude Code channels) are undated in the results, so competitor list is left empty and they are noted here. The Berbix price rests on the Clawvisor launch post quoted on the YC page.
